title: International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy Nutrition
excerpt: Oats, Greek yogurt, lentils, low-mercury salmon, eggs, leafy greens, and citrus — practical ways to build balanced plates.
content:
## Introduction to Pregnancy Nutrition
Pregnancy nutrition is a crucial aspect of the pregnancy process. Expectant mothers need to be provided with adequate nutrients to ensure the health and well-being of both mother and baby. In this article, we will explore international pantry staples that are good for pregnancy, helping to build balanced and nutritious meals.

## International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy
The following are some international pantry staples that are good for pregnancy:
- Oats: rich in fiber, helping to support digestive health and reduce the risk of constipation.
- Greek yogurt: rich in calcium, helping to support the development of bones and teeth for the baby.
- Lentils: rich in iron, helping to support the production of red blood cells and reduce the risk of anemia.
- Low-mercury salmon: rich in omega-3 fatty acids, helping to support the development of the brain and eyes for the baby.
- Eggs: rich in protein, helping to support the development of muscles and tissues for the baby.
- Leafy greens and citrus: rich in vitamins and minerals, helping to support the immune system and reduce the risk of disease.

## Building Balanced Plates for Pregnancy
To build balanced and nutritious meals, expectant mothers can combine international pantry staples with traditional Vietnamese foods. Here are some suggestions:
- Breakfast: oats with Greek yogurt and fruit.
- Lunch: lentils with leafy greens and citrus.
- Dinner: low-mercury salmon with eggs and leafy greens.

## Food Safety Considerations
Expectant mothers need to be mindful of food safety when preparing and consuming international pantry staples. Here are some considerations:
- Choose fresh and clean ingredients.
- Cook ingredients at high temperatures to reduce the risk of bacterial contamination.
- Avoid ingredients that may cause allergic reactions or are not suitable for pregnancy.

## Conclusion
Pregnancy nutrition is a crucial aspect of the pregnancy process. Expectant mothers need to be provided with adequate nutrients to ensure the health and well-being of both mother and baby. International pantry staples like oats, Greek yogurt, lentils, low-mercury salmon, eggs, leafy greens, and citrus can help build balanced and nutritious meals.
